newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares drift down but buyers seen waiting.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares drift down but buyers seen waiting.

text.p: Russian share prices drifted lower on Friday, cooling off after rocketing earlier in the week, traders said, but they said they saw major buyers waiting in the wings for cheaper stock.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed barely down from Thursday at 421.46 after 421.68. Total market turnover was a healthy $58.0 million.
The index had posted six consecutive record closes up to Wednesday, when profit-taking stopped the rise at 433.12 on a record volume of $94 million.

"People are letting the market cool off a little so as to buy the shares more cheaply," said United City Bank head of securities Dmitry Yevenko. "Although you don't see any big buy orders, there is support from professional participants."
Oil company LUKoil slipped to $19.70 after closing on Thursday on $19.80, while national utility UES eased to $0.3611 from $0.3650.

Traders said a decision by Sberbank shareholders, announced after market close on Thursday, to limit ownership by non-residents to five percent of capital pushed the share price down to $286.00 from $299.00.

Rinaco Plus head of securities Andrei Kukk did not see the market rising in the short term. "But if enterprises continue to show good results, then sometime in a month or two the market will go up," he said.
